origin: A real Codex CLI rollout, reduced to the event kinds the parser reads. Redacted by field allowlist: token counters are verbatim, diffs keep their line markers with the code replaced, a created file keeps its line count.
method: Counted from the raw JSONL by a second implementation written against the rollout's shape, never calling internal/parser.

derivations.records: 10 token_count events whose cumulative counters advanced. Codex reports running totals, so a turn is a delta between consecutive events, not the event's own numbers.
derivations.input_tokens: sum of the per-turn input deltas with the cached part taken out. total_token_usage.input_tokens is the whole prompt and cached_input_tokens the share of it served from cache, so the two stored classes have to add back up to the input delta -- 39,772 + 288,256 = 328,028, the total input the counters advanced by.
derivations.cache_read_tokens: sum of the per-turn cached_input_tokens deltas, clamped to the input delta they are part of.
derivations.output_tokens: sum of the per-turn output_tokens deltas.
derivations.reasoning_tokens: sum of the per-turn reasoning_output_tokens deltas. It is a part of output, never added to it.
derivations.cache_write_tokens: Codex publishes no cache-write counter; its depth row does not claim the signal.
derivations.cache_write_1h_tokens: no cache write, so no tier of one.
derivations.lines_added: 217. Three file changes, all to one path: an 'add' carrying a 196-line body, then diffs contributing 19 and 2 '+' body lines. A creation carries the whole file instead of a diff, so a diff-only reader counts 196 of these as zero -- which is what this parser did until v0.13 (B119) and what the Claude Code parser did until v0.14.
derivations.lines_removed: 21 '-' body lines: 19 in the first update diff and 2 in the second. A '-' inside a hunk is a removed line; the '--- a/x' file header before the first hunk is not, which is the distinction a removed line of SQL or Lua depends on.
derivations.rework_lines: 21. All three file changes touch the same path: the window creates it with a 196-line body, then two later diffs remove 19 and 2 lines from it. Every one of those removals undoes a line this window itself added, which is what rework means -- removing pre-existing code is churn, not rework. The first adjudication of this trace said 0 because it had not checked that the three changes were one file; the parser was right and the count is corrected here rather than in the code.
derivations.edits: 3 applied file changes in one patch_apply_end event per change.
derivations.tool_calls: 3. Codex records a patch application rather than an edit-tool call, and each applied file change is one such call. Its depth row claims ai.tool_calls.count, so this is a figure the source supports.
derivations.rejected: Codex does not record tool-use denials -- a documented gap, not a zero.
derivations.tool_errors: Codex marks failures only for file edits, which its depth row deliberately excludes.
derivations.compactions: no compaction boundary in this window.
derivations.skipped: every line is valid JSON and every payload is a shape the parser knows.
derivations.steps: 3, all of them edits. This trace was captured before the reading existed and holds only the event kinds it then needed, so it carries no response_item line at all -- no turn is opened and no named call is made. Each of the three patch_apply_end events applies to one file and contributes one step.
derivations.step_outcomes: 3. patch_apply_end states whether it applied, and all three succeeded.
derivations.step_targets: 3. All three name the same path, so all three carry the same target integer -- which is exactly the shape a repeat-edit reading is looking for: one file returned to three times.
